description:
Define "this dependency is met" once in the domain layer and route every consumer through it, eliminating the Done-vs-terminal drift between blocking, blocked-reason reporting, transition errors, and rendering.

## Background

The rule (dependency met = target state is terminal: Done or Rejected) lives in `Issue::is_blocked` (`domain/types.rs:586`) but is re-encoded independently: `query_blocked`'s reason enumeration tests `!= Done` (`domain/queries.rs:219`), `blocking_dependencies` re-implements the predicate for transition errors (`commands/issue.rs:421-435`), `output.rs:1200` re-derives unmet dependencies for rendering, and `claim_next` inlines the ready predicate (`commands/issue.rs:1088`) instead of calling `query_ready`. The `BlockingReason::Dependency` doc comment says "anything other than Done", contradicting the actual rule.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: One domain helper expresses dependency satisfaction; `is_blocked`, the blocked-reason enumeration, transition blockers, and unmet-dependency rendering all call it.
- [hard] REQ-2: A Rejected dependency is treated as met on every surface (blocked query reasons, issue show output, state transitions), each covered by a test.
- [hard] REQ-3: Next-issue claiming selects via the domain ready-query predicate; the inline copy is gone.
- [hard] REQ-4: Doc comments state the terminal-state rule; no comment or help text describes the rule as "not Done".

## Notes

This is behavior-preserving for `is_blocked` itself; the observable fix is in reason reporting where a Rejected dependency was previously listed as blocking. Sweep for stale narrative in the same change.
title: Unify the dependency-met predicate across all surfaces
